transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um... well, what brings me in is that I just keep making myself throw up after I eat. I do it a lot. Sometimes I even do it in the bathroom at the dry cleaners where I work, or right when I get home. I just... I hate it, but it's started feeling like the only way I can calm down after eating.
When you make yourself throw up, does this usually happen after you eat a large amount of food at once, or do you do it after normal-sized meals as well?

It's usually after a really large amount of food all at once. When it happens, I can just... I'll go through a full bag of chips, some pastries from the corner store, whatever leftovers are in the fridge, and a bunch of sweet drinks. I eat it all in just one sitting, and honestly, I don't even really notice how much is gone until I'm already finished.
During these times when you eat a large amount of food all at once, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control how much you're eating, even if you want to?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Once I start... it feels like my hands just keep reaching for the food, even while I'm in my head telling myself to stop. It's like I'm just watching myself do it, and I can't make myself quit no matter how much I want to.

You mentioned you make yourself throw up after eating. When you do this purging, is it always after those episodes where you feel like you can't stop eating, or do you sometimes do it after normal meals too?

Um... well, it's pretty much always after those times when I just can't stop eating. I don't really do it after a normal meal, like if I just have a regular sandwich or something. It's only when I lose control and eat all that food at once that I feel like I have to go throw it up.
How often does this happen — these episodes where you eat a large amount of food and then throw up? Are we talking a few times a week, every day, or something else?

Um, it's been going on for months now, really. I'd say most weeks have at least a couple of episodes where I just eat way more than I meant to. And then I have to try to undo it. Usually that means throwing up, like I said, but sometimes I try to make up for it by fasting or just exercising it all off.
When you're eating all that food at once, or when you're thinking about purging afterward, how much of it is driven by worry about your weight or how your body looks?

It's... pretty much all of it, honestly. How my body looks is just constantly on my mind. Like, I can be doing really good at work at the dry cleaning shop, keeping up with all the orders, and I'll still feel like a total failure if I just catch my reflection in the glass and my stomach or my hips look big to me. It just ruins my whole day. So yeah, all the throwing up and the fasting... it's all because I'm just terrified of gaining weight and I hate how my shape looks.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with recurrent episodes of binge eating (consuming large quantities of food with loss of control) followed by purging through self-induced vomiting, occurring at least twice weekly over several months. The binge-purge cycle is driven by preoccupation with body weight and shape. These features are diagnostic of Bulimia Nervosa, binge-eating/purging type (F50.02). The purging occurs regularly in response to binges, distinguishing this from non-purging bulimia (F50.01).
